content.title: About
content.content: Green cooked peppers are mature fruits of sweet pepper that are briefly heat‑treated (blanched or boiled) after harvest. The process retains a vivid color, soft texture, and most of the vitamins while reducing bitterness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green peppers are harvested before full ripeness, making them less sweet than red or yellow varieties.
Heat treatment improves digestibility and lowers certain antinutrients.
Cooked green peppers are used worldwide in soups, stews, and salads.
Peppers belong to the Solanaceae family, along with eggplant, tomato, and potato.
Vitamin C retention is better in gently cooked peppers than in raw ones if they are not over‑cooked.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: One cup of cooked green pepper provides over 150 % of the daily vitamin C requirement, supporting immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Carotenoids such as beta‑carotene and lutein protect cells from oxidative stress and promote eye health.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: 100 g of cooked green pepper contain about 20 kcal, making it an excellent choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and normal blood pressure.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to peppers, ranging from skin rash to swelling.

items.title: Potential nitrate content
items.content: Improper storage can lead to nitrate accumulation; it is best to consume fresh, properly stored product.

items.title: Gastro‑intestinal sensitivity
items.content: People with acid reflux or gastritis may find cooked peppers irritating.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked green peppers can be added to soups, stews, pasta dishes, salads, or used as a sandwich filling. They also freeze well when diced for later use.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked peppers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in portioned bags – they retain flavor and nutrients for up to 3 months.
